verdicts.claim: [13] A direct call to PrimePools alone is NOT SUFFICIENT - the gate is inside the callee; the prerequisite is opening the gate first, i.e. GameState+0x898 = 1
verdicts.reasoning: FIRST HALF CONFIRMED: the gate call at 0x33560C5 precedes every functional block, its false arm is 0x33560EF `e9f1030000 jmp 0x33564E5` straight to the epilogue (and the verbosity-suppressed variant 0x33560D6 `jb 0x33564E5`), and nothing in the pre-gate block or in either argument can influence the gate, whose first act is a constant-returning fold. SECOND HALF REFUTED as the identified prerequisite. My exhaustive disp-0x898 scan (see claim [7]) found that the ALokiGameState constructor already writes `mov byte [rdi+0x898], 1` at 0x5676F10, unconditionally — verified by checking that of the 402 instructions in the 0x5676AA0..0x56773FD chain, zero branches span that address and zero indirect jumps exist. So the byte is 1 by native default and 'poke GameState+0x898 = 1' is very likely a NO-OP. The same scan shows the byte is READ in exactly one place image-wide (0x5636438, the gate), so nothing else clears it. Since the 'Feature is not enabled' line was observed live, the false result must instead come from one of the four EARLIER bail conditions in 0x56363F0 (GetOuter() null at 0x5636405, GetWorld() null at 0x563640A, [World+0x258] null at 0x5636416, or the IsA(ALokiGameState) test failing at 0x563642C) — or from a Blueprint GameState subclass overriding the property in class defaults, which is permitted by the flags (CPF_Edit set, CPF_DisableEditOnInstance set) but is [S], not shown.
verdicts.correction: 'The gate is inside the callee, so a direct call still early-returns' is CONFIRMED. 'The prerequisite is GameState+0x898 = 1' is REFUTED as the identified blocker: [M] the native constructor already sets it to 1 on every path (0x5676F10, no branch spans it), and [M] the byte has exactly one reader image-wide. Which of the five conditions actually fails is UNRESOLVED offline and is the real open question.

verdicts.claim: [18] The ActorPoolManager.cpp translation unit is fully enumerated by its string band, and it contains no 'spawn one pooled actor without priming' entry point
verdicts.reasoning: Every individual attribution reproduces EXACTLY via strxref xref: 'Priming pool with %d %s instances.' + 'PrimedActor%s%d' -> fn 0x33585C1 EXACT (606 B); 'Reached primed actor creation time budget (%f)...' -> fn 0x3360395 EXACT (430 B); 'Creation of primed actors is complete.' -> fn 0x3360587 EXACT (83 B); "Can't return actor of type %s to the pool..." -> fn 0x335E241 EXACT (413 B) AND fn 0x3360F30 EXACT (383 B); 'Adding %s to list of poolable actors.' -> fn 0x3359D20 EXACT (3737 B) AND fn 0x335ABCF EXACT (703 B). Base slot 93 = 0x335F890 = `48837a0800 cmp qword [rdx+8],0` / `0f95c0 setne al` / `c3 ret`, multiplicity 1; Loki override 0x5640390 (multiplicity 1) and its first act is `call 0x335F890` — i.e. it chains the base filter. WHAT IS UNSUPPORTED is the word 'fully'. The method is linker string-adjacency, not a TU boundary: the __FILE__ literal 0x7F14A40 itself has refs=0 (it is reached only through the log RECORDS at +0x08, never by a lea), so nothing anchors the band to the TU, and any function in that TU with no string literals is invisible to the enumeration. 'Contains no spawn-without-priming entry point' is therefore an argument from an incomplete list.

summary:
I re-ran every command and re-read every load-bearing byte. Of 22 claims: 12 CONFIRMED, 9 DOWNGRADE, 1 REFUTED.

THE HEADLINE REFUTATION — claim [13], and it changes the lane's next action:
[M] The ALokiGameState constructor already sets bSupportsActorPoolPriming to 1. I ran an exhaustive capstone-validated scan for every memory access at displacement 0x898 across the whole decrypted .text (298 raw candidates, 286 validated instructions — the agent's regex only caught modrm reg-field=eax and so missed this) and found a second unconditional writer at 0x5676F10: `c6879808000001 mov byte ptr [rdi+0x898], 1`. It sits in a straight-line run of field initialisers inside the chained function 0x5676AC3..0x5676FCC, whose later fragment holds 0x56772CF `mov byte [rdi+0xa44], r12b` — the write CLAUDE.md already attributes to the ALokiGameState constructor, on the same rdi. Of the 402 instructions in the 0x5676AA0..0x56773FD chain, ZERO branches span 0x5676F10 and there are no indirect jumps, so it executes on every path. The same scan shows the byte has exactly ONE reader image-wide (0x5636438, the gate).
⇒ "The prerequisite is GameState+0x898 = 1" is REFUTED: that poke is very likely a no-op. Since the "Feature is not enabled" line WAS observed live, the false must come from one of the four earlier bails in 0x56363F0 (GetOuter null / GetWorld null / [World+0x258] null / IsA(ALokiGameState) false), or from a Blueprint GameState subclass overriding the property in class defaults (permitted by the flags, but [S]). Which one is the real open question, and it is answerable with one read-only RPM at runtime.

TWO THINGS I STRENGTHENED BEYOND THE AGENT:
- Claim [6]: I bound the property to its OWNING CLASS, which the agent never did. 0x8983A50 is an element of a 155-entry PropPointers array (0x89847A0..0x8984C70) referenced from the FClassParams at 0x8985478, whose ClassNoRegisterFunc field at 0x8985450 holds rva 0x5380690 — the function whose only strings are U'ALokiGameState' / U'/Script/Loki'.
- Claim [9]: 0x567A1B0 is vtable slot [119] of ALokiGameState, and CLAUDE.md independently records slot 119 = AActor::BeginPlay. That makes the identity [M] by vtable slot, not merely by an inlined profiler literal.

THE MIS-GRADES WORTH ACTING ON:
- [9] quotes bytes that are NOT at the address given: 0x3840490 does not begin `mov rax,[rcx+0x428]` — it begins `mov r11,rsp; push rdi; sub rsp,0xf0` plus a security cookie, with the +0x428 load at +0x1D. This is exactly the "byte string printed next to an address it did not come from" failure.
- [19] is the weakest claim: BOTH cvar strings read refs=0, so nothing in the decrypted image registers or reads `Pooling.PrimingFrameBudget`, and the stated link to fn 0x3360395 is contradicted — that function is xref'd by a different string (0x7F14970). A cvar name in .rdata is not a lever. [S], not [M].
- [3] the verbosity bytes are solid (and I found a layout control at 0x9F7EDD0 reading `05 00 05 07` that the agent did not have), but the NAME "LogActorPooling" is [I]: find_riprel over all of .text returns ZERO references to the string at 0x7F10720 and there are ZERO qword pointers to it image-wide.
- [18] "fully enumerated by its string band" is unsupported — the __FILE__ literal itself has refs=0 (reached only through log records), so string adjacency is not a TU boundary.
- [12] the zero-module-image-write conclusion is CONFIRMED mechanically (no rip-relative memory destination anywhere in the 1284 bytes), but the write list undercounts by seven heap-buffer stores.
- [5], [14], [20] are all sound bytes with names/conclusions graded [M] that are really [I]; note 0x12C7260 has 2,823 pointer occurrences and is non-identifying by address.

FOLD DISCIPLINE: I reproduced the agent's VA counts exactly and identically in all three images (unit: 8-byte LE occurrences at any alignment in the 178,130,944-byte file) — 0xB9E1F0 → 26,444; 0xF7EC20 → 165,789; 0xF7EB50 → 27,217; 0xF7EB60 → 106,924; 0x56363F0 → 1; 0x3356000 → 0. Loki overrides 0x563B170, 0x5640390, 0x566FF50 and setter 0x53800D0 are all multiplicity 1, i.e. none is a fold.

STANDING CAVEAT the claim set should carry: 45–47% of .text is undecrypted, so [8]'s "exactly one caller" and [19]'s refs=0 are lower bounds / coverage-bounded, never ABSENT.
